text:
maria.p: FYI I’m seeing a spike in reconnects from eu-west clients since last deploy. A lot of them are layered: client reconnect -> immediate resume -> duplicate token billing markers.
kevin.r: ugh. any pattern in the resume payloads? are clients sending resume_id or just re-authing?
adele_oncall: logs show mix — ~60% include resume_id, ~40% re-auth with auth header. 401s then immediate retry loop.
maria.p: pasted sample log: 
```
INFO 2026-03-18T09:12:11Z session=abc123 reconnect type=resume resume_id=rs_9f2 attempt=1 route=eu-west sticky=false
WARN 2026-03-18T09:12:12Z session=abc123 auth=failed status=401 retry=immediate
INFO 2026-03-18T09:12:13Z session=abc123 reconnect type=newauth token_id=tok_77 route=eu-west
```
sam.t: looks like proxy sticky-routing gave up when resume failed, then client reconnected to a different shard — that can create duplicate billing if both sessions get accepted briefly.
maria.p: correct. also console shows per-route token counts inflated because we attribute both connections.
console-dev: we can show an extra column in the sessions table: reconnect_method (resume|reauth|replay) and a de-dup flag. easy UI change but need backend telemetry first.
kevin.r: telemetry change request: emit resume_outcome enum (success, invalid_token, session_expired, kv_miss) with server-side resume_id echo. That lets console join events reliably.
adele_oncall: granular resume_outcome helps ops alerts too. But be careful about sensitive fields in logs — echo only hashed resume_id.
sam.t: short-term mitigation: on the server side, when we accept a reconnect with resume_id, mark previous ephemeral session as terminated and reject concurrent accept within 5s window to avoid double-billing. That reduces churn without client updates.
maria.p: agree. we should also surface a UX note in Console rollout: "Sessions accepted on resume will temporarily block duplicate accepts for 5s to avoid billing duplicates" — visible in rollout changelog.
kevin.r: longer term we should add resume_id idempotency in the API layer and a deterministic sticky-routing hint: prefer shard that originally served session_id if resume failed less than 30s ago.
adele_oncall: question on metrics: do we have existing gauge for "concurrent_accepts_per_resume_id"?
maria.p: nope, can add a meter. propose: counter.resume_attempts, counter.resume_concurrent_accepts, hist.resume_latency.
console-dev: once telemetry is in place I can add charts and a small alert rule (>=3 concurrent accepts in 1m).
deploy-bot: <deploy queued: rollout/streaming-resume-mitigations v1.2.3 to prod; ETA 2h>
sam.t: small note: keep the window configurable per-tenant — enterprise customers might want different behavior for low-latency vs strong idempotency.
maria.p: good call. config flag: resume_concurrency_window_ms, default 5000. add to Dedicated/Private configs.
kevin.r: also add a migration plan: emit resume_outcome v1 first (no behavior change), then ops toggle to activate server-side block, then UI rollout. Staged so we can roll back quickly.
adele_oncall: I’ll draft incident playbook snippet: how to detect and roll back if billing duplicate rate increases after change.
maria.p: timeline? can we get telemetry PR today and backend guard in tomorrow’s patch?
sam.t: yes — telemetry PR in 3hrs, backend guard in tomorrow morning deploy. I’ll annotate code with TODO to make window tenant-configurable.
kevin.r: I’ll write the console query for the new chart once telemetry is merged.
maria.p: thanks team. tagging: @adele_oncall for runbook, @console-dev for UI. :thumbsup:
